name: KX3
subtitle: Field reference
kicker: Independent reference. Not an Elecraft publication and not affiliated with Elecraft.
verified: Compiled from the Elecraft KX3 Owner's Manual rev C5, its errata rev C5-4, and the Elecraft product page, September 2026. Not checked against a radio.
specs: 1.5 to 32 MHz general coverage, 0.31 to 1.5 MHz reduced, plus 6 m
160 through 6 m. 2 m or 4 m with the optional module
SSB, CW, data with four sub-modes, AM, FM
10 W on most bands, 8 W on 12, 10 and 6 m. Current firmware raises this to 15 W on 80 through 20 m above 12.8 V supply
9 to 15 V DC. 12 to 14 V for full output
1 to 3 A, varying with band, supply and load
BNC for 160 through 6 m. The VHF module has its own SMA
ACC1 jack, 3.5 mm, serial through a KXUSB or KXSER cable
keys: Held together about two seconds, this is the power switch.
Tap picks the mode. Hold picks the alternate: CW reverse, or the other sideband.
Tap enters data mode. Tap again to step the sub-modes.
Tap swaps the VFOs. Hold reverses them temporarily.
Tap picks 1 or 10 Hz. Hold gives the coarse rate. A long hold locks VFO A.
Tap enables the offset. Hold CLR to zero it.
Tap selects low cut or high cut on voice, width or shift on CW and data. Hold normalises.
Audio peak on CW, auto notch on SSB and AM. Hold NTCH for the manual notch.
Keyer speed in words per minute on CW, mic gain on voice. Hold it to reach the power setting.
Sidetone pitch, VOX or break-in delay, and compression. Holding PITCH on FM turns on the repeater tone.
Key the transmitter, send a tuning carrier, or start a tuner cycle.
Hold to enter. The offset knob scrolls entries, VFO A edits the value.
quick: Mutes mic audio below a threshold.
Voltage at which the low battery warning appears. Worth setting for the pack you actually use.
Backlight on or off. It costs current.
filters: PBT I/II sets low and high cut on voice, width and shift on CW and data. Hold to normalise.
Optional analog module, 3000 Hz and 1000 Hz, selected automatically from the mode and filter settings.
Audio peaking filter for weak CW.
Blanker for impulse noise, reduction for hiss.
tasks: Hold STORE, then rotate VFO A to the memory you want.
Hold RCL, pick the channel with VFO A, tap any key to exit.
Put the start and end frequencies in VFO A and B, then hold SCAN.
Hold the KEYER / MIC knob to reach PWR, then rotate.
control: KXUSB to a computer USB port, KXSER to a real RS-232 port
Set with the BR command. The choices are 4800, 9600, 19200 and 38400. Write yours below.
ACC2, 2.5 mm, is a keyline and logic output. It is not a control port.
The KX3 Utility is needed for configuration and firmware, and gives a CW and data terminal.
notes: Fifteen watts out of a set of AA cells is a short conversation. Plan the power source around the mode and the length of the outing, not around the maximum the radio will make.
The AA socket is a real field advantage because cells can be bought anywhere. Log which chemistry you used: alkaline and nickel metal hydride behave differently under a keyed load.
Six meters is on this radio. Worth a listen on a summer afternoon before you pack up.
The base manual dates from 2014 and the errata does not. If a setting on your radio does not match this page, the errata is the document to read.
The internal tuner is an option. Know whether yours has one.
